metadata.notes: Hand-curated seed data from the original Australia spreadsheets and AU deal listings, plus live rows fetched from the chains that publish a reachable menu API (Pizza Hut, Red Rooster, Oporto, GYG, Carl's Jr) by scripts/fetch_menus.py. Live rows carry a `generatedBy` key, a `channel` of Pickup or Delivery, and the `storeLabel` they were priced at; rows without those keys are hand-curated counter prices. Prices are Queensland-specific and come from the single store nearest the location the fetcher was run with (see metadata.liveFetch). User edits are stored in localStorage and can be exported/imported as JSON.
metadata.audit: McDonald's, Pizza Hut, Red Rooster, Oporto, GYG and Carl's Jr rows are fetched live; KFC, Domino's, Subway and Grill'd remain hand-curated because those chains expose no reachable read API. Pickup and delivery are stored as separate rows because roughly half of all items are priced differently between the two, sometimes by more than double — use the Order type filter rather than mixing them. Oporto publishes kJ on only about 54% of its menu and Carl's Jr publishes no price at all, so those rows are intentionally incomplete rather than dropped. GYG energy is joined from data/gyg_nutrition.json and applies to the grilled chicken build; other fillings are priced but left without energy. Prices vary by store, channel, app account and time — check the chain's own app before relying on them.

Notes & Method
PRICES: Taken from the attached GYG national menu (the ‘from’ / base price for each item).
GYG prices vary by location, ordering channel (in-store vs delivery apps) and over time, so treat these as a guide.
NUTRITION: From the GYG Allergen, Ingredient & Nutritional guide, ‘current at June 25, 2024’.
Serve size (g), energy (kJ) and protein (g) are taken directly from that guide.
Energy (Cal) is calculated as kJ / 4.184.
FILLING: To compare like-for-like, the standard filling is Grilled Chicken where a choice exists.
Exceptions: Quesadilla = cheese only (its base price); $3 Taco = ground beef (only option);
Tender items = crispy chicken tender; corn-chip/queso/fries sides use the dip/seasoning noted.
Brisket adds ~$1 and other fillings shift weight/energy slightly, so value rankings move a little by filling.
METRICS:
Grams / $  = serve size (g) / price  ->  the literal ‘most food per dollar’ measure (headline).
kJ / $     = energy (kJ) / price      ->  most energy per dollar.
Protein g / $ = protein (g) / price  ->  most protein per dollar.
CAVEAT: Grams/$ rewards heavy, dip- or cheese-laden items (e.g. queso fries, corn chips + guac).
For a balanced, filling meal, look at items that rank well across all three metrics — the Enchilada,
Burrito and Bowl are strong all-rounders; Queso Fries and loaded Corn Chips win pure weight-per-dollar.
All value columns are live Excel formulas, so you can edit any price or serve size and rankings update.
McSmart Meal corrected from user-provided AU structure: fixed Cheeseburger + Small Fries, one allowed food option, and one allowed small drink.
McDouble is not an allowed McSmart option and was removed from McSmart meal rows.
McSmart kJ values use the user's supplied component kJ values. Serve grams/protein are only included where all food components are known; drink grams/protein are excluded.
Used Frugal Feeds AU menu/deal listings for public menu/deal prices where original spreadsheets did not include meal deals. Deal prices can vary by store, app and campaign.

Used kfcmenuprice.au current AU menu listing for KFC item prices and energy kJ. Serve grams/protein were not available in the scraped source, so those fields are left null and rendered as unavailable.
Price and kJ arrive together from the product endpoint, so no separate nutrition step is needed.
One row per product size. Hand-entered Frugal Feeds rows are replaced only where the live feed carries the same item name; the rest are kept.
Prices are integer cents in the feed and are converted to dollars on ingest.
The HIDDEN category and products explicitly flagged not visible are filtered out; products are deduped by PLU.
Combo kJ looks unreliable in places (a box with a drink can report less energy than the box alone) — spot-check against the published nutrition guide.
Same Craveable platform as Red Rooster, different host.
kJ is published on only about 54% of visible items and Oporto publishes no nutrition table, so the rest are listed with price only.
Delivery pricing is not a flat uplift on pickup — some items are cheaper on delivery.
The API serves prices but essentially no energy data, so kJ/serve/protein are joined from data/gyg_nutrition.json.
Those figures describe the grilled chicken build, so they are only attached to grilled-chicken (or no-choice) items; other fillings keep price and show no energy.
Mild and spicy variants are collapsed into one row since they are identically priced.
